newsitem.title: UK: Western oil refinery margins up but Asia stumbles.
newsitem.headline: Western oil refinery margins up but Asia stumbles.

text.p: Profit margins at oil refineries around the world rose last week except in Asia where a short upwards spurt petered out and the pattern reverted to its two-month long downtrend.

At least three refinery run cuts last month helped boost margins in Rotterdam by around 45 cents a barrel on average last week when compared with the previous week, according to Reuters calculations employing standard refinery yields.

Rotterdam margins for a complex cracking refinery averaged $1.66 a barrel in May, compared with $2.32 in April. The average for last week was $1.68 but well above a two and a half month low of $1.03 hit on May 23.
Margins for U.S. Gulf coast refiners using imported North Sea Brent crude oil rose by some 16 cents last week to $1.90.
These now stand well above last years average of just 98 cents a barrel.

But analysts fear margins in the U.S. peaked in mid-April, a month or so earlier than in previous years, because of the later-than-usual refinery maintenance programme at the end of last year. At one point in early April, Brent margins stood at around $3.20.
Refiners in the Mediterranean gained some solace from an improvement of 45-50 cents a barrel on average last week in both complex and simple hydroskimming margins to $1.82 and 11 cents respectively.
And in Asia, while margins for the average of last week rose, a sharp fall at the end of the week meant they were barely better by Friday.
Margins for simple hydroskimming refineries in Singapore were calculated to have fallen by three cents or so from the previous Friday to a figure of -46 cents.
For complex refineries they rose by eight cents or so over the same period to around $2.05.
This performance compares to the heady days in early April when margins were at one point well over $6 a barrel.
